citation.authors: Agatha M, Breckenridge C, Soyemi EA

cited_by.title: Kola nut: caffeine, the heart and health claims

record.design: Laboratory observation of aqueous kola nut extract on blood pressure and heart
record.finding: Low doses raised blood pressure by 8 to 9% and high doses lowered it by 18 to 71%. With larger doses a slow heart rate developed and cardiac arrhythmias occurred as a terminal event. The authors say the effects are probably due to caffeine and that the role of habitual chewing in heart disease needs discussion.
record.note: A preliminary animal study from 1978; the doses are not comparable with chewing a nut.
